newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM/PHILIPS PLAN DATABASE WITH DUTCH-US CUSTOMS.
newsitem.headline: KLM/PHILIPS PLAN DATABASE WITH DUTCH-US CUSTOMS.

text.p: KLM Cargo , Philips Electronics and Dutch and U.S. Customs are jointly developing a pilot database system to speed communications between them on Dutch-U.S. air shipments.

The latest edition of KLM Cargo's Cargovision magazine said the four organisations are working on a database computer system which it is hoped will come into operation sometime in 1997. No cost details were given.
The system, which will not be available to other firms, would enable Philips to make a single customs declaration on the planned database for each U.S.-bound shipment.

KLM Cargo, part of KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV, would be named as legal principal for all U.S.-bound shipments, and U.S. and Dutch customs would have comprehensive access to the large, shared database containing all information relevant to the U.S. shipments.
Large companies such as Philips have nothing to hide from customs and a shared database system should mean both customs organisations can facilitate trade, the article added.
